name: Achan
charge: Israel trespassed in the accursed thing: Achan saw, coveted, took of the devoted spoil of Jericho, and hid it in his tent
summary: Who committed the trespass? The first sentence says the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, for Achan took of it. One man’s secret sin sent faintness into the hearts of the whole nation, and thirty-six died before Ai; the Lord said Israel had sinned, and He would not be with them until the accursed thing was destroyed from among them. Taken by lot, Achan confessed that he saw, he coveted, he took: he was stealing from the Most High. He and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor.
offenseFull: The children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, for Achan of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel (Joshua 7:1). Many will answer that Achan committed the trespass; the record says the children of Israel. A man’s individual sins can hurt the rest of the nation. He can be the hindrance to why his camp is not growing, why his family, his marriage or his children have issues, when he carries a spirit he knows about and keeps it secret, not praying and not fasting over it. That is the spirit of Achan, and the nation pays for it, because wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good (Ecclesiastes 9:18).

Joshua had charged them plainly at Jericho to keep themselves from the accursed thing, for all the silver, gold and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated to the Lord and went into His treasury, and nobody was to gain personally from that war (Joshua 6:18-19). Achan’s confession gives the sequence: he saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels, then he coveted them, took them, and hid them in the earth in the midst of his tent (Joshua 7:20-21). He was not stealing from men; he was stealing from the Most High, and he found the time to do it in the middle of a war. Covetousness is the last of the ten commandments, the weightiest warning kept for last (Exodus 20:17), and there is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man, for he sets his own soul to sale (Ecclesiasticus 10:9).
judgmentFull: Confident after viewing Ai, they sent about three thousand men, who fled before the men of Ai; thirty-six fell, and the hearts of the people melted like water (Joshua 7:2-5). The Lord is the one who wins the battles, not us: however strong Israel is physically, if the people are not right with Him He will make them lose, because this fight is not carnal. Hearts melting is the curse written for disobedience: a faintness sent into their hearts, so that the sound of a shaken leaf chases them and they fall when none pursues (Leviticus 26:36). Joshua tore his clothes and fell before the ark until evening, afraid the Canaanites would cut off their name, and asked what the Lord would do for His great name (Joshua 7:6-9).

The Lord told him to get up: Israel had sinned, transgressed the covenant, stolen, dissembled, and put the accursed thing among their own stuff; therefore they could not stand before their enemies, and He would not be with them any more unless they destroyed the accursed from among them (Joshua 7:10-12). It does not say Achan sinned; it says Israel. As a father who finds mischief chastens all his children together when none confesses, so the Most High deals with His children as one house. The lot narrowed by tribe, then family, then household, then man by man, and Achan was taken; Joshua told him to give glory to the Lord God of Israel, make confession, and hide nothing (Joshua 7:16-19). It was a secret sin and no man had seen him, but no man can hide himself in secret places where the Lord does not see him (Jeremiah 23:24), and be sure your sin will find you out (Numbers 32:23).
Joshua and all Israel took Achan, the silver, the

garment, the gold, his sons and daughters, his cattle, his tent and all he had to the valley of Achor; Joshua asked why he had troubled them and said the Lord would trouble him that day, and all Israel stoned him and burned them (Joshua 7:22-25). Why the whole household? The teaching asks it and answers it: they had to have known about it, and they said nothing, so none of them was innocent. A man who sees sin or hears of sin has to speak up, because silence is agreement. They were destroyed for lack of knowledge (Hosea 4:6), and that knowledge is the law, which the priest’s lips are to keep and the people are to seek at his mouth (Malachi 2:7). The law bound a witness who had seen or known of a sin to speak, or bear the iniquity himself (Leviticus 5:1): had they kept the law, they would not have been silent. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God (Hebrews 10:31). They raised over him a great heap of stones, the Lord turned from the fierceness of His anger, and the place was called the valley of Achor to this day (Joshua 7:26).

lawsResolved.text: You shall not covet anything that is your neighbor's.
Abstain from every evil thing when at war against your enemies.

text.text: But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
And ye, in any wise keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed, when ye take of the accursed thing, and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it.
But all the silver, and gold, and vessels of brass and iron, are consecrated unto the Lord: they shall come into the treasury of the Lord.
And Achan answered Joshua, and said, Indeed I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and thus and thus have I done:

When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it.
Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.
Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one setteth his own soul to sale; because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels.
And Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth–aven, on the east side of Beth–el, and spake unto them, saying, Go up and view the country. And the men went up and viewed Ai.

And they returned to Joshua, and said unto him, Let not all the people go up; but let about two or three thousand men go up and smite Ai; and make not all the people to labour thither; for they are but few.
So there went up thither of the people about three thousand men: and they fled before the men of Ai.

And the men of Ai smote of them about thirty and six men: for they chased them from before the gate even unto Shebarim, and smote them in the going down: wherefore the hearts of the people melted, and became as water.

And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.
And Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of the Lord until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads.

And Joshua said, Alas, O Lord God, wherefore hast thou at all brought this people over Jordan, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? would to God we had been content, and dwelt on the other side Jordan!
O Lord, what shall I say, when Israel turneth their backs before their enemies!
For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land shall hear of it, and shall environ us round, and cut off our name from the earth: and what wilt thou do unto thy great name?
And the Lord said unto Joshua, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou thus upon thy face?

Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff.

Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.
So Joshua rose up early in the morning, and brought Israel by their tribes; and the tribe of Judah was taken:
And he brought the family of Judah; and he took the family of the Zarhites: and he brought the family of the Zarhites man by man; and Zabdi was taken:
And he brought his household man by man; and Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.
And Joshua said unto Achan, My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession unto him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me.
Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the Lord. Do not I fill heaven and earth? saith the Lord.
But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.
So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran unto the tent; and, behold, it was hid in his tent, and the silver under it.
And they took them out of the midst of the tent, and brought them unto Joshua, and unto all the children of Israel, and laid them out before the Lord.

And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor.
And Joshua said, Why hast thou troubled us? the Lord shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones.

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.
And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
And they raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day. So the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger. Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day.

Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff.
